passage:
A historic courtroom became a public museum. The wooden chairs, judge's desk, and witness stand were still there.
Students visited during a civics lesson. The guide explained how laws, evidence, and testimony were used in the past. He also pointed out unfair practices that had changed over time.
A student asked why the museum showed mistakes in the justice system.
The guide said, "Because justice improves only when people remember where it failed."
The courtroom felt serious, even without a trial. It reminded students that laws are not just words in books. They affect real people, and they must be questioned, protected, and improved.
